Topics · One God, one message

Hasn't religion caused most wars?

Many wars were fought in God's name, Muslims among them. What does the text say about killing one person?

Part 1 of 3

﴿فَطَوَّعَتْ لَهُۥ نَفْسُهُۥ قَتْلَ أَخِيهِ فَقَتَلَهُۥ فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ ٱلْخَـٰسِرِينَ٣٠ فَبَعَثَ ٱللَّهُ غُرَابًا يَبْحَثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لِيُرِيَهُۥ كَيْفَ يُوَٰرِى سَوْءَةَ أَخِيهِ ۚ قَالَ يَـٰوَيْلَتَىٰٓ أَعَجَزْتُ أَنْ أَكُونَ مِثْلَ هَـٰذَا ٱلْغُرَابِ فَأُوَٰرِىَ سَوْءَةَ أَخِى ۖ فَأَصْبَحَ مِنَ ٱلنَّـٰدِمِينَ٣١ مِنْ أَجْلِ ذَٰلِكَ كَتَبْنَا عَلَىٰ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ أَنَّهُۥ مَن قَتَلَ نَفْسًۢا بِغَيْرِ نَفْسٍ أَوْ فَسَادٍ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَكَأَنَّمَا قَتَلَ ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًا وَمَنْ أَحْيَاهَا فَكَأَنَّمَآ أَحْيَا ٱلنَّاسَ جَمِيعًا ۚ وَلَقَدْ جَآءَتْهُمْ رُسُلُنَا بِٱلْبَيِّنَـٰتِ ثُمَّ إِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِّنْهُم بَعْدَ ذَٰلِكَ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لَمُسْرِفُونَ٣٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

And his soul permitted to him[256] the murder of his brother, so he killed him and became among the losers. Then Allāh sent a crow searching [i.e., scratching] in the ground to show him how to hide the disgrace[257] of his brother. He said, "O woe to me! Have I failed to be like this crow and hide the disgrace [i.e., body] of my brother?" And he became of the regretful. Because of that, We decreed upon the Children of Israel that whoever kills a soul unless for a soul[258] or for corruption [done] in the land[259] - it is as if he had slain mankind entirely. And whoever saves one[260] - it is as if he had saved mankind entirely. And Our messengers had certainly come to them with clear proofs. Then indeed many of them, [even] after that, throughout the land, were transgressors.[261]

Translator's notes

[256] i.e., the killer allowed himself.

[257] Referring to the dead body, evidence of his shameful deed.

[258] i.e., in legal retribution for murder. [259] i.e., that requiring the death penalty. [260] Or refrains from killing. [261] Heedless of Allāh's limits, negligent of their responsibilities.

Quran · Al-Ma'idah 5:30-32

Translation

Rescue those who are being led away to death! Indeed, hold back those who are staggering to the slaughter!

Original · Hebrew

הַ֭צֵּל לְקֻחִ֣ים לַמָּ֑וֶת וּמָטִ֥ים לַ֝הֶ֗רֶג אִם־תַּחְשֽׂוֹךְ׃

Proverbs · 24:11

World English Bible

Begin with what is not in dispute: people have killed in God's name, often, in many traditions, Muslims included. How large a share of wars this makes up is argued among historians. The deeper question is whether the text orders it. These verses tell of a killing between two brothers. Then they draw a rule: whoever unjustly kills one soul, it is as if they killed all humanity. What accounting of blood is heavier? One victim counts as the whole human race.

A question for you

When someone kills in God's name, where do you see the first cause?

If you sayIn religion itself
ThenThat view deserves its weight. To test it you would need to separate what a text commands from what its followers do, and that comes next.
If you sayIn leaders who use it
ThenThat comes close to what the next verse describes, and it does not excuse followers.
If you sayIn human nature
ThenThen war would find another cause without religion. The Quran itself records the angels' concern about bloodshed (2:30).

Part 2 of 3

﴿وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يُعْجِبُكَ قَوْلُهُۥ فِى ٱلْحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنْيَا وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَلَدُّ ٱلْخِصَامِ٢٠٤ وَإِذَا تَوَلَّىٰ سَعَىٰ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ لِيُفْسِدَ فِيهَا وَيُهْلِكَ ٱلْحَرْثَ وَٱلنَّسْلَ ۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْفَسَادَ٢٠٥﴾

Translation of the meaning

And of the people is he whose speech pleases you in worldly life, and he calls Allāh to witness as to what is in his heart, yet he is the fiercest of opponents. And when he goes away, he strives throughout the land to cause corruption therein and destroy crops and animals. And Allāh does not like corruption.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:204-205

Translation

His mouth was smooth as butter, but his heart was war. His words were softer than oil, yet they were drawn swords.

Original · Hebrew

חָלְק֤וּ ׀ מַחְמָאֹ֣ת פִּיו֮ וּֽקֲרָב־לִ֫בּ֥וֹ רַכּ֖וּ דְבָרָ֥יו מִשֶּׁ֗מֶן וְהֵ֣מָּה פְתִחֽוֹת׃

the Psalms · 55:21

World English Bible

The critic is on firm ground saying God's name is used as a cover. These verses describe it exactly: a man whose speech impresses you, who calls God to witness what is in his heart, and who, once he has power, strives to ruin, destroying crops and lives. The Quran does not say whoever mentions God is innocent. It exposes this very man. A text that foresees this picture is not holding him up as its model.

A question for you

How would you tell a sincere faith from a faith used as a cover?

If you sayBy what it does to the weak
ThenA strong test, and the verse agrees: crops and offspring. You can apply it to every group, your own included.
If you sayI cannot tell them apart
ThenAn honest place to be. It may help to judge the teaching rather than the people, which has a question of its own.
If you sayEvery religion is a cover
ThenIf that held, the word "sincere" would have no use here. You might ask what you are measuring by.

﴿وَقَـٰتِلُوا۟ فِى سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ ٱلَّذِينَ يُقَـٰتِلُونَكُمْ وَلَا تَعْتَدُوٓا۟ ۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ ٱلْمُعْتَدِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Fight in the way of Allāh those who fight against you but do not transgress. Indeed, Allāh does not like transgressors.

Quran · Al-Baqarah 2:190

﴿ٱلَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا۟ مِن دِيَـٰرِهِم بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّآ أَن يَقُولُوا۟ رَبُّنَا ٱللَّهُ ۗ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ ٱللَّهِ ٱلنَّاسَ بَعْضَهُم بِبَعْضٍ لَّهُدِّمَتْ صَوَٰمِعُ وَبِيَعٌ وَصَلَوَٰتٌ وَمَسَـٰجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا ٱسْمُ ٱللَّهِ كَثِيرًا ۗ وَلَيَنصُرَنَّ ٱللَّهُ مَن يَنصُرُهُۥٓ ۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَقَوِىٌّ عَزِيزٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

[They are] those who have been evicted from their homes without right - only because they say, "Our Lord is Allāh." And were it not that Allāh checks the people, some by means of others, there would have been demolished monasteries, churches, synagogues, and mosques in which the name of Allāh is much mentioned [i.e., praised]. And Allāh will surely support those who support Him [i.e., His cause]. Indeed, Allāh is Powerful and Exalted in Might.

Quran · Al-Hajj 22:40

The Quran does permit fighting in defence, and that must be said. It also has hard verses on war, with a question of their own. So what limits does it set? The first verse: fight those who fight you, and do not overstep. The second gives a reason: without some people defending against others, monasteries, churches, synagogues and mosques would be pulled down. Houses of worship of different faiths, named side by side as what is defended. You can measure religious people's acts by this text.

A question for you

What would you need to know from history before answering this question for yourself?
